findings.detail: The subject is the bare gene but the polarity is that of its loss-of-function variants (in the note only), so read as subject-relation-object the steps say TREM2 lowers Abeta phagocytosis and INPP5D raises inflammation; curated inverted.

INPP5D leads_to (negative) 'PI3K pathway suppression' says INPP5D raises PI3K signaling, the opposite of its own note, of the H3 mechanism ('suppresses PI3K activation') and of H1.2's note; the H3 INPP5D arm composes with the wrong sign.

INPP5D's UniProt entry (Q92835), which the run cites at H1.2 (inflammation), not at H3.3, says INPP5D is 'negatively regulating the PI3K ... pathways', refuting H3.3 as signed; H3.3 itself cites only an OT score and a STRING edge, so the agent cited the text that states the PI3K step at the wrong step.
Each step starts at a different gene (TREM2, INPP5D, PLCG2, ABI3) and no object is the next subject: four parallel single-gene claims, only ABI3's reaching the disease.

H2.1 ends at brain cholesterol, H2.2 restarts at APOE, H2.2 ends at TREM2 signaling and H2.3 restarts at PLCG2; no step links APOE epsilon4 to Alzheimer disease, whose risk appears only in H2.1's note.
H3.1 ends at TREM2 signaling and H3.2 restarts at MS4A4A; H3.2 ends at immune receptor signaling and H3.3 starts at INPP5D ('downstream of MS4A4A' is only in the note).
H3 never reaches Alzheimer disease and states no direction for MS4A4A on it; it ends at PI3K signaling, so it was curated with claims on its end nodes only.
H1's title and mechanism give no per-gene direction; only the falsification test does (knockout of TREM2, INPP5D, PLCG2 worsens pathology), and it is about pathology, not risk.

Ten of the 27 step citations are Open Targets records (association scores or a safety-liability list) and two are STRING text-mining edges; none can state a direction, and they appear to fill the two-sources-per-hypothesis budget.
Neither PMID:28714976 nor PLCG2's UniProt text mentions calcium signaling or immune activation by PLCG2; the step has no support.
ABI3 leads_to AD cites an INPP5D/RIPK1 paper, a review that lists ABI3 without direction, and an OT score; the two citations were usable only for other steps (H1.1, H1.2).
Nothing cited mentions epsilon4 and cholesterol together; the rs429358 GWAS row names no allele ('rs429358-?') and is about age of onset, so it cannot even give epsilon4's direction.
No cited text gives APOE's effect on TREM2 signaling; UniProt makes APOE a TREM2 ligand and says ligand binding triggers signaling, so the run's negative sign has no stated basis.
'Protective PLCG2 variants delay onset' is written as leads_to but its only paper reports a Cox/Kaplan-Meier association of variants with onset age; no cited text tests PLCG2's effect.
The step about the APOE4 isoform is grounded to the APOE protein (UniProtKB:P02649), so the allele the hypothesis is about is lost from the node.

The 'Microglia' context has an empty CURIE and is grounded with HPA:ENSG00000168918, which is INPP5D's expression record, on steps about TREM2, ABI3, APOE and MS4A4A; most process objects also have empty CURIEs.
The mechanism says MS4A4A is 'expressed in microglia', but the cited HPA record (ENSG00000110079) lists cDC, Hofbauer cells, Kupffer cells and macrophages, not microglia.

PMID:PPR987754 is listed as contradicting H3, but it contradicts no H3 step: it shows Ms4a4a loss reduces plaque burden in 5xFAD, while H3 gives no direction for MS4A4A on the disease; its 'more pro-inflammatory' Ms4a4a-null microglia also match no step.

GWAS rows rs75932628-T (TREM2, OR 2.22), rs72824905-G (PLCG2, OR 0.73) and rs616338-T (ABI3, OR 1.31) give allele directions, but no step is about a variant; STRING:INPP5D-PLCG2 and HPA:ENSG00000168918 also state no step.
HPA:ENSG00000130203 (APOE expression) states no step.
rs983392-A (OR 1.11, author-reported gene MS4A6A) and HPA:ENSG00000110079 state no step; no step links MS4A4A to the disease.

All three hypotheses are labelled support 'grounded' (confidence 'low'), yet of 27 step citations only 2 state their own step; 2 more state other steps (PMID:41633359, PMID:41315858, both cited at H1.4) and 1 (Q92835, cited at H1.2) refutes another step (H3.3).
RNPS1 and LPIN2 are reported as unexplained and appear in no hypothesis.

BLN:APOE-epsilon4: the corpus has NCIT:C105364 'Apolipoprotein E4', but render.py's PREFIX_KIND has no NCIT entry so it cannot be used; PR has no isoform term and the allele is a two-SNP haplotype with no single dbSNP ID.

terms.py finds NCIT terms (NCIT:C105364 'Apolipoprotein E4') but render.py rejects them as 'a term of unknown kind', so the guide's 'BLN only when nothing in any ontology fits' cannot be met and a local term was forced.

No rule lifts a functionally characterised variant's association to its gene: PMID:41620758 says P522R 'encodes a mildly hyperactive form' and is protective, which implies PLCG2 activity lowers risk, but strictly this is association_only for a gene-level effect step.
'PLCG2 variants offset APOE epsilon4 risk' is effect modification; a condition refinement (PLCG2 in epsilon4 carriers) holds it only as a separate node, cut off from the PLCG2 claims of H1.

One PMID:41435829 span mixes macrophage, microglia (in vitro), non-human-primate and mouse work; an evidence row has one kind and one taxon, and the taxon list has no primate, so it was recorded as mechanistic, mouse.
PMID:41633359's abstract never names its species; 'mouse' was inferred from its mouse-style gene symbols (Nlrp3, Zbp1) and aging/motor phenotypes, and evidence rows have no field to say so.

HP has only circulating cholesterol terms; the species-neutral UPHENO:0051760 'brain cholesterol level phenotype' ('a changed level of cholesterol in the brain') fits a human step better than the mouse MP:0012779, but the guide's undirected-change rule names only HP and MP.
The run's object is TREM2 signaling (activity), but PMID:41435829 shows lower TREM2 protein (amount); kept as activity, the curator decides that the amount change counts.

Whether an H1 claim composes depends on its aspect: the cited bridge (phagocytosis reduces AD pathology) is severity, so TREM2 composes only because the falsification test speaks of pathology; with risk it would have no route.
The run puts 'Microglia' on most steps as a run-wide setting; BioLean has no run-level context, so it was dropped everywhere rather than refining every node.

The mechanism says 'rare coding variants in TREM2, INPP5D, PLCG2, and ABI3', but the cited rare-variant study (PMID:28714976) names rare coding variants in PLCG2, ABI3 and TREM2 only, and no cited text or GWAS row names any INPP5D variant.

The only direction for ABI3 in any cited text, the risk variant rs616338 p.Ser209Phe (OR 1.43), is in PMID:28714976, which the run cites at the PLCG2 step H1.3, not at the ABI3 step H1.4; it is an association, so it could not support the leads_to step anyway.

The falsification text describes a simultaneous knockout of TREM2, INPP5D and PLCG2, while its structured perturbation names TREM2 only; a triple knockout gives no direction for each gene on its own, so the per-gene H1 claim signs taken from it are an inference.

render.py does not check an evidence row's ref against the step's own citations or its moved_from, so Q92835 (cited at H1.2) sat under H3.3 without moved_from and the first curation called it H3.3's own citation.
